newsitem.title: CHINA: China bank chief sees foreign banks in renminbi.
newsitem.headline: China bank chief sees foreign banks in renminbi.

text.p: China wants to open its financial markets further and the next step is to allow foreign banks to conduct local currency business, the head of the central bank was quoted as saying.
The China Securities newspaper quoted Dai Xianglong, governor of the People's Bank of China, as saying the move would be limited to a specified location.
He did not say which location would be chosen for foreign banks to be allowed to accept deposits and make loans in local currency, the renminbi.
Shanghai's Pudong district has frequently been mentioned as the most likely financial centre for such reforms.
Foreign banks are now not permitted to conduct renminbi business.
Dai gave no timetable for the move.

China has been talking about allowing foreign banks into the domestic market for some time, but foreign bankers and economists have raised doubts about Beijing's willingness to liberalise the market anytime soon.
They say that domestic banks, already under pressure from new Chinese financial institutions, are reluctant to see even more competition from big foreign banks.
